discovery: The jamming transition: a unifying framework for rigidity and flow in disordered matter
motivation: Liu and Nagel showed that very different disordered systems, including granular packings, foams, emulsions, colloids and glasses, lose or gain rigidity through one common jamming transition. Their jamming phase diagram and the identification of point J as a critical point with isostatic marginal stability revealed universal scaling laws. These include power-law growth of the contact number and moduli, a diverging length scale, and an excess of soft vibrational modes that explains the anomalous low-temperature properties of glasses. The framework turned the old question of why amorphous solids are rigid into a predictive physics of marginal solids. It now guides work on shear thickening in dense suspensions, the rheology of tissues and cells, and tunable mechanical metamaterials built by pruning bonds. Their later work on physical learning in materials came from the same program. Jamming is one of the most influential concepts in condensed matter physics of the past three decades.
